title: Anaheim Convention Center Transportation | Luxury Limo
description: Planning an Anaheim Convention Center event? Compare SUVs, Sprinter limos, and shuttles, plus airport transfer times and exhibitor logistics that matter.
h1: How to Arrange Luxury Transportation for Anaheim Convention Center Events

blocks.text: For most convention schedules, book a black SUV or sedan for executives, a Sprinter limo for teams of 8 to 14, and a shuttle loop for anything larger. The Anaheim Convention Center sits across from Disneyland, which means the roads around it are busy even when your show is not.

blocks.text: Why Convention Transportation Is a Different Job

A wedding runs late and everyone forgives it. A trade show does not. Badge pickup opens at 8, your booth briefing is at 8:30, and the keynote starts at 9. If the car is 20 minutes late, three people miss the briefing and you spend the morning apologizing.

blocks.text: The Anaheim Convention Center is the largest convention center on the West Coast, with 1.6 million square feet of space and more than a million visitors a year. When a large show is in town, the hotels along Convention Way and Katella Avenue fill up, and the drop-off lanes get crowded. A pre-arranged vehicle with a driver who knows the building is not a luxury. It is schedule insurance.

blocks.text: Pick the Vehicle by Job, Not by Headcount

rows: Sprinter limo plus a cargo run, or a small bus

blocks.text: The mistake we see most is booking a Sprinter for 14 people who each brought a booth kit and a roller bag. The seats fit. The bags do not. Tell us the box count when you book and we will size accordingly, or arrange a separate materials run.

blocks.text: Exhibitor Logistics: the Part Nobody Warns You About
Limos and party buses do not pull into the loading dock. Freight has its own access, its own schedule, and usually its own union rules. If you are exhibiting, plan three separate movements:
blocks.html: Limos and party buses do not pull into the loading dock. Freight has its own access, its own schedule, and usually its own union rules. If you are exhibiting, plan three separate movements:

items: The crew and their personal bags, from hotel to hall, before the floor opens.
The booth materials, through the official freight channel or a cargo van, not the passenger car.
The client dinner or after-show event, from the hall to the restaurant and back.

blocks.text: Build 20 minutes of buffer into the first morning. Badge pickup, a security check, and a hall that is bigger than it looks on the map will eat it.

blocks.text: Now the parking math. Ten colleagues driving in separately is ten $25 entries, ten cars looking for a space in a 1,000-space lot, and no way to leave for lunch without paying again. blocks.text: Getting From the Airport to the Convention Center
John Wayne Airport is about 14 miles and 20 minutes from the convention center. LAX is about 35 miles and 45 to 75 minutes, depending on the 405. If you have a choice, fly into SNA.

blocks.text: Where the Car Meets You

The convention center has two published passenger zones, and neither is the main lobby curb. Rideshare, taxis, and shuttles use the Transit Plaza on the south side near Hall E, or the Convention Way entrance by Morton's Steakhouse on the north side. Buses and oversized vehicles approach from West Street off Katella, which keeps them out of the tighter pedestrian corridor.

blocks.text: Which one you use depends on your hall. If your show is in the Arena, the bus zone is off Arena Plaza via Hotel Way. If it is in the north halls, Convention Way is closer. Send your chauffeur the hall name and the show name, not just the street address. We confirm the pickup point the day before and the driver texts when he is staged.

blocks.text: Multi-Day Shows: Book the Week, Not the Morning
If you are in town for a three-day expo, a daily car is the wrong model. Book a dedicated vehicle and driver for the block, or set a standing schedule with the same driver each morning.

blocks.text: Booking Checklist for Event Planners

items: Send the show name, hall, and daily start and end times, not just the address.
Give the hotel address for every pickup. Groups often stay across three properties.
Confirm headcount and bag or box count separately.
Ask where the vehicle stages during the day, and whether waiting time is billed.
Confirm the overtime rate before the show, because sessions run long.
Name one on-site contact who can approve changes by text.
For multi-day events, ask for a written schedule with driver and vehicle details for each day.

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
How far is the Anaheim Convention Center from John Wayne Airport?
About 14 miles, typically 20 minutes. From LAX it is roughly 35 miles and 45 to 75 minutes depending on traffic.
blocks.html: About 14 miles, typically 20 minutes. From LAX it is roughly 35 miles and 45 to 75 minutes depending on traffic.

blocks.text: Can a party bus drop off at the convention center?
Yes, at the designated passenger loading area. Large vehicles cannot use the freight dock, and some shows restrict where buses may stage, so confirm the pickup zone for your event.
blocks.html: Yes, at the designated passenger loading area. Large vehicles cannot use the freight dock, and some shows restrict where buses may stage, so confirm the pickup zone for your event.

blocks.text: Do you provide shuttles between hotels and the convention center?
Yes. We run scheduled loops between Anaheim hotels and the convention center in Sprinters, party buses, or charter buses, depending on the group size.

blocks.text: What is the best vehicle for a corporate group of 10?
A Mercedes Sprinter limo. It seats up to 14, has stand-up headroom, and carries laptops and luggage far better than a stretch limo.

blocks.text: Can you handle airport pickups for a whole delegation?
Yes. We coordinate multiple vehicles and staggered arrivals, track each flight, and meet attendees at baggage claim.

blocks.text: How early should I book convention transportation?
Two to four weeks for a normal show. For a large convention, or any date during a major citywide event, book six to eight weeks out.
